items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A thirsty crow found a pitcher with only a little water at the bottom, too low to reach. One by one, the crow dropped pebbles into the pitcher until the water rose to the top and she could drink.

What is the theme of this fable?
items.answer: The theme is that clever thinking can solve a hard problem. The crow uses pebbles to raise the water instead of giving up.

steps: The crow cannot reach the water at first.
She drops pebbles until the water rises.
The lesson is that thinking cleverly solves problems.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Luca bragged that he never needed to study. On the day of the big test, he stared at the questions and could not answer a single one. His friend Mara, who studied a little every night, finished with a smile.

What lesson does this story teach?
items.answer: The lesson is that steady preparation matters more than bragging. Luca did not study and failed, while Mara studied a little each night and did well.

steps: Luca brags and does not study.
He cannot answer the test, but Mara, who studied, does fine.
The theme is that preparing beats boasting.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The whole soccer team wanted to be the star. They each tried to score alone and kept losing the ball. Their coach taught them to pass, and once they shared the ball, they finally started to win.

What is the theme of this story?
items.answer: The theme is that working together as a team leads to success. The players kept losing until they shared the ball and cooperated.

steps: Each player tried to score alone and they lost.
After learning to pass, they started to win.
The lesson is that teamwork brings success.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Jade told a small lie about breaking a vase, blaming the cat. To keep the story going, she had to tell more lies, and soon she could not keep them straight. In the end she felt so tangled and miserable that she told her mother the whole truth and felt lighter at once.

What is the theme, and how does the ending show it?
items.answer: The theme is that honesty brings relief while lies only pile up and weigh you down. Jade's one lie forces more lies until she feels miserable, and telling the truth makes her feel "lighter at once."

steps: One lie leads Jade to tell more and more.
She feels tangled and miserable.
Telling the truth makes her feel lighter, showing honesty is better.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

On moving day, Sam had to leave the tree house he and his best friend had built. He was sure their friendship would end. But they wrote letters, video called on weekends, and by summer had planned a whole week together. The miles between them never shrank their friendship.

Write a one-sentence summary of the story.
items.answer: When Sam moves away and fears losing his best friend, the two stay close through letters and video calls and plan to spend a week together.

steps: Identify the key events: Sam moves and worries about the friendship.
They keep in touch and plan to reunite.
State it in one sentence without opinion.

items.prompt:
Read the poem.

The river does not fight the stone,
It bends and slips around.
And year by year the patient stream
Wears mountains to the ground.

What life lesson, or theme, does this poem suggest?
items.answer: The theme is that patience and gentle persistence can overcome even the biggest obstacles. The river does not fight the stone but slowly wears down mountains over time.

steps: The river bends around the stone instead of fighting.
Over years it wears mountains down.
The lesson is that patient persistence beats force.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Every kid in class avoided the grumpy old neighbor, Mr. Boyd. But when his mail piled up, Tomas knocked to check on him and found Mr. Boyd had hurt his ankle. Tomas ran errands for him all week. Slowly, Mr. Boyd began waving to the other kids, and his frown softened into a smile.

What is the theme of this story?
items.answer: The theme is that kindness can change people and break down walls between them. Tomas's care turns the grumpy neighbor into someone who waves and smiles.

steps: Everyone avoids the grumpy neighbor.
Tomas helps him when he is hurt.
The neighbor becomes friendly, showing kindness can change people.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Priya wanted the lead in the school play so badly that she hoped her rival would forget her lines. But at the audition, when her rival froze, Priya quietly whispered the next line to help. Her rival got the part, yet the director gave Priya a special role for her kindness. Priya realized helping had felt better than winning.

Write a short summary, then state the theme.
items.answer: Summary: Priya wants the lead role and hopes her rival fails, but when her rival forgets a line, Priya helps her; the rival gets the part while Priya earns a special role for her kindness. Theme: Being generous and helping others can be more rewarding than winning.

steps: Summary: retell the main events in order and briefly.
Priya helps her rival instead of letting her fail.
Theme: helping others feels better than winning, as Priya learns.

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A farmer's son complained that the family's small field would never make them rich. "Dig deeper," his father said, "and you will find our treasure." The son dug the whole field looking for gold and found none, but the loosened soil grew the finest crop the family had ever sold. Only then did he understand his father's words.

What is the theme, and how do the son's actions reveal it?
items.answer: The theme is that hard work itself is the real treasure. The son digs the field expecting gold and finds none, but his labor produces the best crop ever, which is the treasure his father meant.

steps: The father hints at treasure to get the son to dig.
The son finds no gold, but the digging makes a rich crop.
The lesson is that effort and hard work are the true treasure.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the drought dried up the village stream, each family hoarded its own water and neighbors stopped speaking. Old Mira was different. She left her full bucket at the crossroads with a sign: "For whoever needs it most today." Shamed and moved, others began sharing too, and the village made it through the dry season together.

Write a short summary of the story, then explain its theme.
items.answer: Summary: A drought makes villagers hoard water and stop speaking, but old Mira leaves her bucket for whoever needs it, inspiring others to share so the village survives the dry season. Theme: Sharing and generosity, even in hard times, help a whole community survive.

steps: Summary: the drought divides the village until Mira shares her water.
Her example spreads and the village survives.
Theme: generosity in hard times helps everyone through.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Noah spent all his savings on a shiny store-bought kite that snapped in the first strong wind. His grandfather then helped him build one from newspaper, sticks, and string. It looked plain, but it flew for hours and never tore. "The kite you make with care," Grandfather said, "outlasts the one you only pay for."

What is the theme, and how does the contrast between the two kites support it?
items.answer: The theme is that things made with care and effort can be more valuable and lasting than things simply bought. The expensive store kite snaps quickly, but the plain handmade kite flies for hours and never tears.

steps: The store-bought kite is shiny but breaks fast.
The homemade kite is plain but lasts and flies well.
The contrast shows care and effort outlast money spent.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Every autumn, Dad and I raked the yard into one enormous leaf pile, and every autumn I jumped in and scattered it everywhere. He never got angry. He just laughed and started raking again. Years later, when I raked my own yard alone, I finally understood that the leaves were never really the point.

Write a short summary, then state the story's theme.
items.answer: Summary: A child scatters the leaf pile every autumn while the patient dad only laughs and rakes again, until years later, raking alone, the grown child realizes the raking was about spending time together. Theme: The time we spend with the people we love matters more than the task we are doing.

steps: Summary: the yearly raking and jumping is a shared ritual with Dad.
Later, alone, the narrator understands its real meaning.
Theme: shared time together matters more than the chore itself.

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A lion caught a tiny mouse and was about to eat it. "Spare me," squeaked the mouse, "and one day I may help you." The lion laughed at the idea but let the mouse go. Weeks later, the lion was trapped in a hunter's net. The little mouse crept up and gnawed through the ropes, setting the great lion free.

What is the theme of this fable, and how do both animals' actions show it?
items.answer: The theme is that no act of kindness is ever wasted, and even the small can help the powerful. The lion spares the mouse, and later the small mouse repays that mercy by chewing the lion free from the net.

steps: The lion shows mercy by freeing the small mouse.
Later the mouse frees the trapped lion.
Both actions show kindness is returned and the small can help the mighty.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The town's inventor, Odell, built a machine to do every chore so no one would have to work. At first the townspeople cheered. But with nothing to do, they grew bored and lonely, forgetting how to bake, build, or sing together. One by one they switched the machine off and picked up their old tools, and laughter returned to the streets.

Write a summary of the story, then explain the theme in your own words.
items.answer: Summary: Odell builds a machine to do all the town's chores, but with nothing to do the people grow bored and lonely, so they turn the machine off and return to their old work and community. Theme: Meaningful work and doing things together give life joy and connection, so a life with no effort is not truly better.

steps: Summary: the machine removes all work but makes people bored and lonely.
They choose to work again and are happier.
Theme: work and shared effort bring meaning and joy.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The great oak in the schoolyard was scheduled to be cut down for a parking lot. Most people shrugged, but nine-year-old Wren gathered stories from everyone who had ever climbed it, read weddings held beneath it, and taped them all around the trunk. When the crew arrived and read the notes, they set down their saws. Today the oak still shades the yard, its bark papered with memories.

Write a short summary of the story, then state its theme and one detail that supports it.
items.answer: Summary: When the schoolyard oak is set to be cut down, young Wren collects and posts people's memories of the tree, and the moved work crew decides to leave it standing. Theme: One determined person, and the shared value people place on something, can protect what matters. Supporting detail: after reading the taped stories, the crew "set down their saws."

steps: Summary: Wren saves the oak by posting people's memories on it.
The crew reads them and stops.
Theme: one caring person plus shared meaning can protect what matters; the crew setting down their saws proves it.
